articles.title: Before an AI agent acts, decide what it may do
articles.summary: Useful agents need clear limits. Check the tools, account permissions and approval steps before letting software act on your behalf.
articles.imageAlt: A robotic gripper pauses above a brass key on an oak desk beside a green notebook.
articles.imageCaption: AI-generated editorial illustration of an agent and a key; a visual metaphor for permissions, not a real product or event.

claimsChecked.claim: Excessive agency can arise from excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy; least privilege, downstream authorisation and human approval are recommended controls.
Logging and rate limits can reduce damage but do not prevent excessive agency on their own.
Instructions in external files or websites can cause indirect prompt injection.

articles.title: When AI answers from your files, follow the evidence
articles.summary: Document-connected AI can shorten the route to an answer. Its usefulness still depends on the passage, date, context and access behind each citation.
articles.imageAlt: An open book, indexed ivory folders, papers and a magnifying glass on a library table beside a laptop.
articles.imageCaption: AI-generated editorial illustration of books and indexed documents; a conceptual scene, not a photographed office.

sources.text: Microsoft Learn: Retrieval-augmented generation in Azure AI Search

claimsChecked.claim: Grounding connects model output to verifiable sources, reduces hallucinations and supports auditability with links.
RAG faces query understanding, multi-source access, token constraints, freshness and granular access-control challenges; some designs query remote sources.
RAG does not fully mitigate prompt injection vulnerabilities.

articles.title: What an image's Content Credentials can tell you
articles.summary: A signed image history can show useful information about creation and edits. Learn what it establishes, what it leaves open and how to check the claim beside it.
articles.imageAlt: An unbranded black camera, forest photographic prints and a brass loupe on an oak table.
articles.imageCaption: AI-generated editorial illustration of a camera and photographic prints; the prints are generated artwork, not documentary photographs.

sources.text: Google DeepMind: Original SynthID image-watermarking explanation (2023)

claimsChecked.claim: Content Credentials record signed provenance assertions; their validation does not judge whether the provenance information is true.
Metadata can be stripped; soft bindings such as fingerprinting and invisible watermarking can help rediscover associated credentials.
The original 2023 SynthID image system embedded a watermark in Imagen images; Google acknowledged limits under extreme manipulation.
